mcqs.question: A view controller is pushed, popped back to, then pushed again later in the same session. Which callback fires on every one of those three transitions, not just the first?
options: loadView
viewDidLoad
viewWillAppear
None — all of these fire only once per instance
mcqs.explanation: viewWillAppear fires every time the screen is about to become visible, including return visits, while viewDidLoad and loadView fire once per controller instance when the hierarchy is first created.

mcqs.question: A screen fetches its list data only inside viewDidLoad. A user edits an item on a pushed detail screen and pops back. What's the bug, and the fix?
options: There's no bug — viewDidLoad reruns automatically on pop
The list shows stale data because viewDidLoad doesn't rerun; move the refresh to viewWillAppear
The fix is to move the fetch to viewDidLayoutSubviews so it reruns on every layout pass
The bug is unrelated to lifecycle and is caused by Auto Layout caching stale frames
mcqs.explanation: viewDidLoad runs exactly once per instance, so a fetch placed there never re-executes on a return visit; viewWillAppear runs on every appearance and is the right place for data that can go stale between visits.

mcqs.question: You add a custom child view controller with addChild(_:) inside a hand-rolled container and manage appearance transitions manually. What must you do to avoid appearance callback bugs?
options: Nothing — UIKit always forwards appearance transitions automatically for any child
Set shouldAutomaticallyForwardAppearanceMethods to false and explicitly call the child's beginAppearanceTransition/endAppearanceTransition
Override the child's viewDidLoad to call the parent's viewWillAppear manually
Avoid addChild entirely and only use UINavigationController for containment
mcqs.explanation: Manual containment requires explicitly forwarding appearance transitions to children so their viewWillAppear/viewDidAppear fire correctly; UIKit only auto-forwards for its own built-in containers like UINavigationController unless you disable automatic forwarding.

mcqs.question: Code in viewDidLoad reads a view's bounds.width to size a gradient layer and gets 0. What's the correct fix?
options: Force layoutIfNeeded() inside viewDidLoad before reading bounds
Move the sizing code to viewWillLayoutSubviews or viewDidLayoutSubviews, which fire after frames are resolved
Read frame instead of bounds, since frame is always accurate in viewDidLoad
Move the sizing code to viewDidAppear only, since it always fires last
mcqs.explanation: viewDidLoad runs before Auto Layout has resolved real frames, so bounds reads as whatever was set at init, often zero; the layout callbacks fire specifically after the layout engine settles frames. Forcing layoutIfNeeded works but fights the framework instead of using the callback built for this.

mcqs.question: A detail screen is popped from the navigation stack but its deinit never runs, and memory grows on every push/pop cycle. Instruments shows the parent and child mutually retaining each other. Most likely cause?
options: The child has a custom delegate property that isn't declared weak, creating a cycle back to the parent
UINavigationController itself leaks by design and this is expected
The child overrides deinit, which prevents ARC from deallocating it
viewWillDisappear was never called, so the child thinks it's still visible
mcqs.explanation: UIKit's own parent/child containment already uses weak-where-appropriate references; the usual cause of a leak here is application code adding its own strong reference back to the parent, most commonly via a non-weak delegate or callback property. Overriding deinit doesn't block deallocation, and a missing viewWillDisappear call wouldn't by itself create a retain cycle.
